title: She Fell 33,000 Feet Without a Parachute #shorts
description:
Would you ever fly again? 👇

In January 1972, flight attendant Vesna Vulović survived a fall of about 33,000 feet (10,160 m) when her plane broke apart over Czechoslovakia. She was the only survivor of 28 people, and it is still the world record for the highest fall survived without a parachute.
#truestory #survival #planecrash #worldrecord #shorts

beats.text: She fell thirty-three thousand feet. No parachute.
beats.speaker: medic

beats.text: Six miles up, a bomb tears the plane apart. That's the official story.
beats.speaker: narrador

beats.text: Flight attendant Vesna Vulović is trapped in a falling piece of the plane, pinned by a food cart.
beats.speaker: narrador

beats.text: It crashes into a snowy, wooded mountainside.
beats.speaker: narrador

beats.text: Fractured skull. Both legs broken. Three vertebrae crushed.
beats.speaker: medic

beats.text: She woke up in a hospital with no memory of the fall.
beats.speaker: narrador

beats.text: Was she even supposed to be on that flight?
beats.speaker: rep

beats.text: No. The airline mixed her up with another flight attendant… also named Vesna.
beats.speaker: narrador

beats.text: Twenty-eight people on board. One survivor. It's still the world record for the highest fall without a parachute.
beats.speaker: narrador

beats.text: And she never flew again, right?
beats.speaker: rep

beats.text: Wrong. She asked for her job back.
beats.speaker: medic

question: How did she survive a 33,000-foot fall?

analisis_gancho.que_gancho_usan: La cifra brutal del clímax en la primera frase funciona; lo que nos hunde es la ficha de presentación y la pregunta de premisa ("How does anyone survive that?").
analisis_gancho.funcionaria_aqui: Sí, la cifra (33.000 pies sin paracaídas) pasa la prueba del desconocido. Se quita la ficha de 1972 y la pregunta de premisa: se pasa directo a la acción (la bomba, el trozo cayendo) y se guarda el error de la aerolínea como segundo bucle.
